comment: Brian (ElevenLabs) VO for Episode 17 (300s): Spain vs Cape Verde, Group H, real kickoff ~Jun 15 2026. Canon: content/Stories/Spain-vs-Cape-Verde.md (The Empire and the Island). VERIFIED real facts: Cape Verde is a nation of ~525,000 people across ten volcanic islands ~350 miles off West Africa; 2026 is their FIRST-EVER World Cup. For decades the islands exported talent to bigger nations - Henrik Larsson (Cape Verdean father) starred for Sweden, Nani (Cape Verdean descent) for Portugal, Gelson Martins (born in Cape Verde) plays for Portugal - now the islands field their own. Captain Ryan Mendes, long-serving talisman. Spain: 2010 World Cup winners, Euro 2024 champions, ~48 million people. Lamine Yamal, 18-year-old Barcelona prodigy, was photographed as a baby being bathed by Messi in a 2007 charity shoot. Rodri, 2024 Ballon d'Or winner, first defensive midfielder of the modern era to win it. RULES: Ep16 SWE-TUN recap labelled OUR PREDICTION (we predicted 1-1). This ending is OUR PREDICTION (3-1 Spain, with Cape Verde scoring a historic first World Cup goal). Soccer only - round-neck shirts, a pitch with goals, NO helmets/pads. Lines short - never tempo-stretch.

lines.text: Ten volcanic islands in the middle of the Atlantic. Half a million people. For sixty years they sent their sons to play for other people's flags.
Tonight, for the very first time, the islands play for themselves. And on a clifftop back home, a keeper is lighting his lamp.
Last time, we predicted Sweden and Tunisia would draw one-all — frost against fire. Tonight: an empire against an island.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode seventeen. Spain versus Cape Verde. Forty-seven million... against half a million.
And stay with me — because tonight, an island that was never supposed to score... scores.
First, the history. And this one is true. Cape Verde — ten islands, three hundred and fifty miles off the coast of Africa, smaller than a single Spanish city.
For generations the islands were a nursery for the world. Henrik Larsson lit up Sweden. Nani lifted trophies with Portugal. Gelson Martins, born on the islands, played for Lisbon.
The blood was Cape Verdean. The shirts were everyone else's. The islands gave the game its stars... and kept none of them.
Until now. Twenty twenty-six: their first World Cup. Ever. The sons of the islands, finally home, finally in blue.
And the team they meet first? The empire itself.
Spain. Champions of the world in twenty-ten, champions of Europe in twenty twenty-four — the most complete football machine on the planet.
Lamine Yamal. Eighteen years old. The boy once photographed as a baby, bathed by Messi in a charity calendar — now the most dangerous teenager in the world.
And anchoring it all, Rodri. The twenty twenty-four Ballon d'Or — the first defensive midfielder of the modern era to win the game's greatest prize.
A team that does not lose. A teenager who does not fear. But across from them stands a captain who has waited his whole life for this.
Cape Verde. Ryan Mendes — the old leader, the man who carried these islands for over a decade so that this night could exist.
With Garry Rodrigues and his trickery, and a young defence that refuses to believe small nations should be grateful just to be here.
They did not cross the Atlantic to be a footnote. They came to write their own chapter.
So here is the duel. Spain's empire against the islands' dream. The boy who fears nothing... against the captain who waited forever.
Our prediction — built on Spanish class, on island courage, and on one goal that will be sung about for a hundred years. Watch.
Spain come in waves. Yamal collects on the right, freezes three defenders, and curls it home. One-nil. The machine purrs.
And soon, a second — patient, inevitable, Spanish. Two-nil. The empire stretches its legs.
But then — the moment. Garry Rodrigues, a yard of space, a swing of that left boot.
And the islands score. Cape Verde's first goal at a World Cup, ever. Half a million people, somewhere, off their feet at once. Two-one.
Spain answer late — class will tell — and finish it three-one. But nobody in blue is hanging their head.
Three-one to the empire, in our story. But the island left a mark that will never be erased: their first. Their very first.
Do you agree? Comment EMPIRE if Spain are simply too good. Comment ISLAND if Cape Verde's first goal is the moment of the round.
And the keeper with the lamp? Legend number seventeen: the Lighthouse Keeper. For sixty years he kept a light burning for the sons who sailed away.
Tonight they came home, and his light guided them in. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score... scores for you.
Free to play. Live prize pool. Underdogs pay triple — like Cape Verde tonight.
Hit like — send this to the friend who loves an underdog. And subscribe: the legends are only beginning.
